scope: Read-only review of original videos and frozen logs; no new policy inference, simulation, intervention or model modification.

reviewed.fine_review: Paired normal/dim index02 videos 14.0–20.0s at about0.25s intervals. Video time is approximately simulation time minus1s; simulation timestamps are from commands.jsonl.
reviewed.crop_reason: Matches fixed policy crop. Contact sheets are unmodified original frames except crop and text labels.

paired_lighting_outcomes.lighting: Physical scene ambient/diffuse/specular intensity multiplied by0.9; image brightness multiplier remains1. This is only a mild lighting test.

observations: All9 fine failures approach, grasp and lift the red cube. Eight videos visibly carry it into the blue tray, then remain above it without satisfying full-opening completion. This contradicts a blanket claim that these failures could not see or locate the initial cube.

Fine dim index02 loses the cube near the front edge of the tray: video15.2s still carrying;15.5s cube below/front of the gripper;15.8s resting outside the tray. It does not merely run out of time while holding the cube in the air.

Paired normal index02 also loses gripper contact near the tray, but the cube lands inside the tray. Mapping/timing audit: dim last bilateral contact16.32simsec, bilateral loss16.34, table contact16.66; raw and issued gripper targets remain near0.342, so there is no commanded early opening. Better describe this as loss of grip/slip near the tray edge, not active premature release.

Base representative videos index02 and42 in both lights do not execute a successful approach/grasp; they move above/away from the target. These motions alone do not distinguish visual localization error from lack of task-specific visual-to-action adaptation.

visual_cause_assessment.supported: Light changes can alter the policy trajectory; index42 changes outcome and index02 changes failure manifestation. No normally successful position becomes a failed position under this10% light reduction.
not_supported: Claiming allBase failures are caused by not seeing the cube.
Claiming 8 incomplete-opening failures are due to wrong cube/tray localization.
Claiming dim index02 proves a perception error: slip, geometry and learned action policy can explain the observable event, and no localization head/error estimate exists.
Claiming mild lighting pairing proves general visual robustness or no perception contribution.
Using historical22k RGB conditioning test as direct33k failure diagnosis.
visual_cause_assessment.appropriate_wording: 视觉误判目前未被直接证实；图像变化可能是轨迹变化的诱因，但这组失败的直接可见问题主要在后半程握持、入盘和张爪完成动作。

preprocessing_evidence.limits: This verifies the checked pipeline path, not the learned model's semantic localization accuracy in every frame.
